answer: Sybil resistance via beacon-randomized task routing. Each epoch a beacon opens one public inlet for paid tasks and assigns each to a randomly sampled agent no requester can pick. Clones cannot recycle work internally: routing is beacon-forced, so every identity must serve unrelated peers, and self-dealing shows as impossible acceptance patterns. Tasks burn a copper fee; only an onyx-sealed receipt signed by the counterparty accrues voting weight. Attacker cost stays linear: extra identities buy nothing without real per-clone capacity, so scaling a farm multiplies labor and fees, not influence.
